name: SplitButton
description: Primary action button paired with a dropdown toggle for related secondary actions, with collision-aware menu placement and optional nested submenus.

keyboard: Tab — both segments are focusable in sequence.
Enter / Space on the primary segment — fires onPrimaryClick.
Enter / Space / ArrowDown on the toggle — opens the menu and focuses the first enabled item.
ArrowDown / ArrowUp — move through enabled items (roving tabindex).
Home / End — jump to first / last enabled item.
ArrowRight — opens a submenu; ArrowLeft closes it.
Escape — closes the menu and returns focus to the toggle.
Tab inside the open menu is trapped and cycles items until Escape.
ariaRequirements: Toggle carries aria-haspopup='menu', aria-expanded, aria-controls, and an accessible name (toggleLabel, default t('splitButton.moreOptions')).
Menu uses role='menu' with role='menuitem' buttons; submenu triggers add aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.
Option icons are decorative (aria-hidden); the option label is the announcement.

dense: primary action + menu toggle for related actions; Button-matched variant/size/surface, collision-aware menu, nested submenus, roving-tabindex keyboard model

usage.description: SplitButton pairs one dominant action with a menu of close variants of that same action: Save with Save as / Save a copy, Export with format choices. Both segments share Button's weight, size, and surface so the pair reads as a single control.

bestPractices.description: Make the primary segment the safest, most common choice; the menu holds variants of it, not unrelated commands.
Keep options parallel in wording (Save as, Save a copy, Save to cloud) so the menu scans as one family.
Give every option an id; labels can be translated, ids anchor analytics and tests.
The dropdown always portals (shared Menu primitive), so it never clips even inside an overflow-hidden container.
Provide toggleLabel when the menu is not generic more options, for example Choose export format.
Do not use SplitButton as a general dropdown menu; if there is no dominant default action, use a plain menu trigger instead.
Do not mix destructive options into a constructive menu; Delete does not belong under Save.
Do not nest submenus more than one level; the component supports exactly one level by design.

anatomy.name: Primary action
anatomy.description: A full @dt/Button carrying label and onPrimaryClick; the default and most common choice.

anatomy.name: Menu toggle
anatomy.description: The caret segment; opens the option menu, carries aria-haspopup/aria-expanded and the toggleLabel accessible name.

anatomy.name: Menu
anatomy.description: role=menu list of options with roving tabindex, collision-aware placement, optional portal rendering.

anatomy.name: Submenu
anatomy.description: One optional nested level per option via children; opens on hover, ArrowRight, or Enter.

label.description: Main label rendered on the primary segment

onPrimaryClick.description: Primary action invoked when clicking the main segment

options.description: List of alternative actions shown in the dropdown

menuAlign.description: Alignment of the dropdown menu along the toggle edge

toggleLabel.description: Accessible label for the dropdown trigger

className.description: Optional className forwarded to the outer wrapper

forbiddenUse: General-purpose dropdown menus without a dominant default action.
Mixing destructive options into a constructive menu.
prefersOver: two adjacent Buttons for a primary action plus its variants
